articles.title: VALLOUREC SHOWCASES ITS VAM® PORTFOLIO AND THE EXTENSION OF ITS CLEANWELL® OFFER AT ADIPEC 2026
articles.description: VALLOUREC SHOWCASES ITS VAM® PORTFOLIO AND THE EXTENSION OF ITS CLEANWELL® OFFER AT ADIPEC 2026 Meudon, France, October 15, 2026 - Vallourec, a world leader in premium seamless tubular solutions, will take part in ADIPEC 2026, the world’s largest energy industry event, taking place from November 2 to 5, 2026, in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. This year, Vallourec will showcase its VAM® offer, as well as its latest solutions designed to enhance performance, operational efficiency and support the energy transformation. A world reference in the Oil and Gas industry since 1965, VAM® continues to set the standards for performance and reliability in the most demanding environments. The comprehensive portfolio of connections meets the requirements of oil and gas applications, as well as geothermal wells, hydrogen and carbon storage projects. Backed by global manufacturing capabilities, tailored services and cutting-edge R&D, the VAM® offer reflects Vallourec’s expertise for complex energy projects. At Vallourec’s booth 3115, located in Hall 3 at ADIPEC 2026, visitors will be able to discover the VAM® 21, and VAM® HTTC connections, as well as Vallourec’s solutions for unconventional applications, including VAM® SPRINT-TC designed to support the development of this major market in the Middle East. The Vallourec® Services offering, covering project engineering, on-site operational support and tube management, will also be presented. ADIPEC 2026 will provide an opportunity to showcase, for the first time, the recently expanded CLEANWELL® range, Vallourec’s dope-free solution. Designed to enhance operational efficiency while reducing the environmental impact, CLEANWELL® is now available on a wider portfolio, including the VAM TOP® connection. Delphy, Vallourec’s worldwide unique solution for underground hydrogen storage, will also be presented. Jérôme Favre, Senior Vice President of the OCTG Services and Accessories Business Line, and Bertrand de Rotalier, Senior Vice President New Energies, Project Line Pipe and Process, will be on site to answer press inquiries. To schedule a press meeting, please contact: Raphaèle Quaranta, Head of Marketing Communications & Sales Support Tél : +33 6 45 09 14 43 raphaele.quaranta@vallourec.com About Vallourec Vallourec is a world leader in premium tubular solutions for the energy markets and for demanding industrial applications such as oil & gas wells in harsh environments, new generation power plants, challenging architectural projects, and high-performance mechanical equipment. Vallourec’s pioneering spirit and cutting-edge R&D open new technological frontiers. With close to 13,000 dedicated and passionate employees in more than 20 countries, Vallourec works handin-hand with its customers to offer more than just tubes: Vallourec delivers innovative, safe, competitive and smart tubular solutions, to make every project possible. Listed on Euronext in Paris (ISIN code: FR0013506730, Ticker VK), Vallourec is part of the CAC Mid 60, SBF 120 and Next 150 indices and is eligible for Deferred Settlement Service. In the United States, Vallourec has established a sponsored Level 1 American Depositary Receipt (ADR) program (ISIN code: US92023R4074, Ticker: VLOWY). Parity between ADR and a Vallourec ordinary share has been set at 5:1. For further information, please contact: Press relations - Taddeo Romain Grière Tel: +33 (0)7 86 53 17 29 romain.griere@taddeo.fr Attachment PR_ADIPEC_Vallourec 2026

articles.title: Currie Slams 'Vibe' Oil Contracts As Trump Admin Halts SPR Drains, IEA Urges Massive Reserve Release
articles.description: Currie Slams 'Vibe' Oil Contracts As Trump Admin Halts SPR Drains, IEA Urges Massive Reserve Release Oil prices are extending gains again this morning as traders weigh a weaker global demand outlook and signs of recovering Middle East crude supplies against persistent shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz and escalating/spreading violence between the Houthis and Saudis. An overnight lull in prices (set with hopes for more reserve releases) was upset as Iran showed more clips of tankers/container ships under attack. The International Energy Agency said Wednesday that Gulf crude shipments rose by 4.4 million barrels a day to 13.9 million barrels a day in September, reaching more than 75% of prewar levels. Global oil supply increased by 2.5 million barrels a day to 102.3 million barrels a day, driven by Gulf producers. However, the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping, the agency said. Given the massive crude draw reported by API (likely impacted by shut-ins from the first Atlantic hurricane of the year in the US Gulf), all eyes are on the (Columbus Day-delayed) official data... API Crude -11.1mm Cushing +1.8mm Gasoline +1.1mm Distillates -1.5mm DOE Crude -8.56mm Cushing +1.86mm Gasoline +3.52mm Distillates -2.52mm HUGE CAVEAT - the shut-ins in the Gulf make this very noisy: Confirming API's reporting, the official data showed a large crude draw last week (and another sizable draw in distillates inventories) while stocks at Cushing and overall Gasoline inventories saw builds... For the first time since the Iran war began, the Trump admin did not drain any reserves from the SPR... US Crude Production tumbled last week (shut-ins in the Gulf, so not comparable)... Total US Diesel stocks remain at seasonal record lows... WTI has surged up to $97.50 However, watching futures is misleading as Wall Street veteran Jeff Currie exclaimed this morning that the world’s most important oil benchmark has become little more than a “vibe contract", blunting its usefulness as a tool to manage price volatility. Brent’s disconnect from physical markets is creating “unpriceable risk,” deterring hedgers from using the contract to protect themselves, Currie said. “Everything associated with energy is going up but Brent,” Currie said Thursday in an interview on Bloomberg Television. “It is not connected to the real world anymore.” A hit to Brent’s integrity undermines the market’s ability to anticipate supply shocks with “profound consequences for the market and the rest of the world,” Currie said. The disconnect between paper and physical markets has frustrated traders since the Middle East conflict began, when crude struggled to top $100 despite historic supply shortages. In contrast, Dated Brent, the most important physical oil benchmark, has surged to near $130 a barrel. That dissonance has contributed to traders fleeing the market, with Brent open interest earlier this month hitting its lowest since March 2025 even as oil dominates headlines. Diesel prices are lower this morning... Finally, Bloomberg reports that US officials attending an International Energy Agency meeting in Paris earlier today informally lobbied allies to commit an additional 100 million barrels from emergency oil inventories to supply global markets. "While US officials attending an IEA gathering in Paris on Thursday have yet to table a proposal about what should be done, they have been informally lobbying for an extra commitment of at least 100 million barrels, the people said, asking not to be identified because the matter is not public." (BBG) The report says US officials believe IEA members have not released enough oil from the coordinated 400 million-barrel oil and fuel release announced in March to cushion the impact of the Gulf conflict. The Group of Seven nations agreed earlier this month to release up to 100 million barrels after President Trump threatened Europeans with a halt to exports of diesel and other petroleum products. Today's request follows Trump's deal with Moscow to supply US and global markets with thousands of tons of diesel fuel. On top of this, a defiant President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times earlier today that his armed forces will attack Russian refineries once again. This comes after the Trump administration requested that Ukraine stop hitting Russian refineries, as those attacks have been one of the drivers of the global refining crisis. Last month, IEA head Fatih Birol said about one-third of the 400 million-barrel release announced in March had been delivered to global markets. Meanwhile, US SPR inventories have fallen to levels not seen since the early 1980s. The Trump administration's scramble comes as midterm elections are just three weeks away. The latest credit and debit card data from Bank of America show that US consumers are spending more on fuel at the pump, crowding out other purchases and weighing on consumer sentiment. Tyler Durden Thu, 10/15/2026 - 12:10

articles.title: RLC Pro AI delivers top AI performance on NVIDIA DGX Spark with Enterprise Linux stability
articles.description: CIQ optimizes RLC Pro AI for DGX Spark with the newest long-term kernel and NVIDIA drivers, so the same Enterprise Linux runs from prototype to production RENO, Nev., Oct. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- CIQ, the enterprise software company behind Rocky Linux, today announced RLC Pro AI (Rocky Linux from CIQ Pro AI) optimized for NVIDIA DGX Spark. Developers get leading AI performance from the newest long-term kernel and NVIDIA's latest validated GPU drivers, on the same trusted, vendor-backed Enterprise Linux that runs business-critical infrastructure. On Spark Arena, the community leaderboard where DGX Spark owners publish reproducible benchmark recipes, a DGX Spark running RLC Pro AI outperformed four common sparkrun tests at up to 10% faster than the leading entry. The challenge developers face is that the operating system they choose for speed is rarely the one their organization runs in production. Development stacks keep up with the newest kernels and drivers, while Enterprise Linux has typically trailed them to protect stability. When a prototype is ready, teams move it to a different operating system and rebuild drivers, containers and dependencies, then check whether the performance survived the move. Every one of those moves delays the point where AI work starts to deliver value. RLC Pro AI closes that gap with one operating system for both sides. It runs the CIQ Linux Kernel 6.18, the newest long-term kernel, with NVIDIA's latest validated GPU drivers to get more from the Spark's Grace Blackwell hardware. When that work moves to production, the speed moves with it, along with the lifecycle stability, security maintenance, and enterprise support production depends on. AI performance starts with the operating system. The software beneath the AI stack decides how quickly a developer can test an idea, evaluate a model, and feed the results into the next experiment, which makes the choice of operating system a practical decision about AI productivity. "Developers have had to pick between the fastest operating system and the one their company trusts in production. RLC Pro AI ends that choice, and provides an optimized, homogenous environment from prototype to production. It puts the newest long-term kernel and validated GPU drivers on Enterprise Linux, and it beat the Spark community's own leaderboard to prove it. Developers get the speed they want on their Spark today, and when that work becomes business-critical, it is already on the operating system enterprises run their most important infrastructure on," said Bjorn Hovland, President of CIQ. Enterprise infrastructure matters from the first experiment. RLC Pro AI brings the lifecycle stability, security maintenance, and commercial accountability of Rocky Linux from CIQ into the development environment, so teams build on the same Enterprise Linux choice they'll rely on as applications grow. RLC Pro AI also works with CIQ Fuzzball, which CIQ previously announced for DGX Spark, to take that work to larger GPU environments for training and inference. Availability RLC Pro AI optimized for NVIDIA DGX Spark is available now. Developers can register for a free RLC Pro AI developer license for their Spark through the CIQ Portal. The developer license is for individuals and covers up to 25 nodes for non-production, non-commercial use. About CIQ CIQ is the founding support and services partner for Rocky Linux and a leading provider of Enterprise Linux infrastructure. CIQ delivers secure, performant software infrastructure for the full range of modern workloads. Global enterprises, government agencies, research institutions and supercomputing centers trust CIQ to run their most advanced workloads in production, from mission-critical environments to the systems behind major scientific and AI breakthroughs. CIQ's products include the Rocky Linux from CIQ (RLC Pro) family of operating systems, Ascender Pro for IT automation, Fuzzball job-based container orchestration, Warewulf Pro cluster provisioning, and Apptainer, the container system built for high-performance computing, with Apptainer Pro coming soon. Learn more at ciq.com. Media contact Christina Roach ciq@offleashpr.com

articles.title: We've tried Apple HomeView, the smart home hub that iPhone owners have been waiting (a long time) for
articles.description: Apple just unveiled its all-new HomeView alongside a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini 2 speaker during an event in New York City. The showcase was designed to demonstrate how Siri AI, rebuilt from the ground up earlier this summer, can become an essential companion in the home. The smarter, more personal assistant has already changed the way we use our iPhone, thanks to its ability to answer complex open-ended questions and draw from the information stored in your text messages and emails to find specific details that would otherwise take hours of scrolling. With a HomeView on your worktop, bookshelf, bedside table, or mounted on the wall, Siri AI can leverage all of those capabilities to manage your schedule, control smart home gadgets, fire up a playlist or podcast, and be a crib sheet for everything stored on your iPhone. GB News was in Manhattan to be one of the first to see how this works in practice. Apple hasn't strayed from its typical formula with the HomeView. That's to say, this is not the first product of its kind, arriving almost a decade after Amazon announced its first-generation Echo Show smart display, but the Apple-built equivalent arrives with an extraordinary level of finish and best serves those who already heavily invested in its ecosystem of products and services. It's also more expensive than the competition, but more on that later. Since HomeView is designed to take a spot inside your home — ideally somewhere that you're able to easily check and swipe its gorgeous seven-inch Liquid Retina display — design is particularly important. The most striking thing about HomeView is how adorable it is. That might sound like an odd thing to say about a gadget, but its small stature and cherubic rounded display ensure there's something incredibly endearing about the HomeView. That touchscreen is connected to the half-dome speaker with a sturdy stainless steel hinge that tilts so you can avoid any troublesome glare. The wall-mounted version drops the speaker in the base and relies only on those around the display to play music. HomeView is surprisingly small, and wouldn't look out of place on a bedside or coffee table. Those who want to gather around as a family to use the Centre Stage camera, which ensures everyone remains in-frame even as they move around, for a FaceTime call might find themselves longing for more screen real estate, as Amazon offers with its Echo Show 11. When it's not in use, HomeView has a series of beautifully designed clock faces. Many of these will be immediately familiar to Apple Watch owners. There are endless customisation options, including the font, colours, and complications to offer weather conditions, world clock, and upcoming calendar appointments at a glance. Between the 1:1 aspect ratio, rounded corners, and shared clock faces with its bestselling smartwatch, HomeView can resemble a supersized Apple Watch. One of the available options will spotlight photos from your library. You can even set a Shared iCloud Album as the source of these photos, so family members or friends can upload recent additions, refreshing multiple HomeViews — even those in different households — with new pictures. Like the Lock Screen on your iPhone, subjects are automatically separated from the background, ensuring the date and time never obscure someone's face. Given most of us have thousands of photos on our smartphones that we never really look at, HomeView could be a nice hassle-free way to be reminded of some choice memories. Like the Apple Watch and Apple TV, Snoopy makes a very welcome appearance on HomeView. There's a series of custom animations that play, with the weather on-screen reflecting the conditions outside. Likewise, Snoopy will celebrate certain holidays — Christmas, for example — on the HomeView at the same time as you. It's a fun addition, and will please younger members of the household and big kids alike. For our money, we would've loved to see the Toy Story cast as well as Micky and Minnie Mouse enjoy their own clock face too, since these Disney staples have all made appearances on the Apple Watch in the past. Likewise, some of the breathtaking aerial footage that serves as a screensaver on Apple TV would look stunning on this photo frame-like display, serving as a digital version of the 1,000 Places To See Before You Die daily tear-off desk calendar. Fingers crossed the teams at Apple regularly refresh the selection of clock faces available on HomeView. Software updates — bringing new features and security fixes — will be delivered via the Home app preinstalled on your iPhone or iPad, like the HomePod smart speakers already available from the brand. HomeView walks a tricky tightrope — it needs to be personal enough to be useful for everyone living under the same roof, but secure and private enough that you're confident allowing it to display your texts or manage your reminders. To solve this, HomeView has several safeguards. First, it boasts facial recognition for up to six people. But that's not enough, so Apple also checks that your iPhone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network (or, failing that, in roughly the same location as the HomeView) and has been recently unlocked. HomeView doesn't come equipped with Face ID — the facial recognition system used to unlock most iPhones and authenticate contactless payments — so the extra precautions ensure someone can't use a photograph to trick the camera and unlock access to your personal data when you're not home. However, its absence is not a case of Apple skimping on components. Face ID works by projecting some 30,000 invisible infrared dots onto your face and checking the unique curves, angles, and distances between your facial features. This isn't a three-dimensional scan, but instead takes the form of mathematical data for all of this geometry. Given that HomeView is designed to be used from across the room, rather than at arm's length — like an iPhone or iPad, this projection system isn't suitable. During our demo, profiles switched over instantaneously whenever someone new walked up to the HomeView. A notification flags when a new profile has been signed in. With so much concern about AI, should you trust Siri to access everything on your iPhone? HomeView has an elegant solution to nosiness from other members of your household. If someone peers at the screen while you're composing a text, for example, the display will automatically lock, GB News was told. This system also serves as a way to make sure everyone enjoys a personalised experience. Like an iPhone, you can customise the appearance and layout of apps and add widgets, so each member of your household can add their own flourish to the device. This all appears the moment that HomeView recognises you. Likewise, playlists in Apple Music, photo libraries, podcasts, and other in-app data will appear when you swipe the touchscreen or use Siri AI on the HomeView. Some experiences — like the ability to customise the colour or brightness of smart lightbulbs, or check a doorbell camera feed — are always accessible to everyone. This isn't entirely new. Both Google Nest and Amazon Echo devices offer personalised experiences, so you can send text messages to your contacts and add items to your calendar, without allowing anyone at home to access. But these services rely on voice recognition to sort you from the rest of your household. Alexa Voice ID data — the acoustic model of your voice characteristics — is stored on Amazon's servers, something that might put you off using this feature. And unlike the HomeView, there's nothing to stop prying eyes. HomeView has a couple of unique tricks up its sleeve too. Handoff lets you beam a song, podcast, or audiobook from your iPhone to the HomeView. Just hold your phone in front of the display, and you'll see a splash animation as if you've physically thrown something into the screen. HomeView will pick-up at the exact spot where you left off. The inverse too, letting you take a song or episode with you when you leave the house. Like the jaw-dropping animation when you open the iPhone Duo, GB News was left seriously impressed with this beautiful flourish. It is impeccably executed and adds to a seamless cohesion between these devices, helpful when you've invested in multiple gadgets from the same brand. Another example of these nice touches is the cooking experience with HomeView. If you find a recipe in its Safari web browser, onboard Artificial Intelligence (AI) will detect that it's a recipe and distil all of the information into an easily digestible, step-by-step format that you can follow in the kitchen when your hands are busy. If the recipe mentions timings, Apple will add shortcuts to kickstart a timer for that designated time. You'll be able to see a countdown in real-time of exactly how long is left at the top of the screen, similar to the Dynamic Island on iPhone. iPhone 18 Pro review HomeView will pull out the list of ingredients too, and using the power of Siri AI, you can ask the chatty assistant to add these to your shopping list, remind you to buy a particular item when you're near the local supermarket. HomeView is available in four colours: Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, Space Grey. However, that drops to just two — Silver and Space Grey — if you choose the wall-mounted version. While both versions of the HomeView cost the same at checkout, the wall-mounted one requires extra hardware to attach to the wall. Apple has created three purpose-built mounts, ranging from £54.95 to £119.95. That makes this a much more expensive proposition, and while the company reassured GB News it has tuned the audio to bounce soundwaves off the wall to preserve audio quality ...the fact that it's missing the drivers in the base must result in a weaker output. Early Verdict There’s no shortage of ways to manage smart lightbulbs, thermostats, or security cameras. And if you’ve ever browsed Amazon during the Black Friday sales, you’ll know the US retailer is prepared to offer some aggressive discounts to tempt you into its own ecosystem, which includes a paid subscription to its smarter Alexa+ assistant, Ring doorbells, and Blink security cameras. Likewise, Google has its own Nest Hub smart display and security cameras. There are standards that mean you can use these devices interchangeably. HomeView supports the two biggest ones: Matter and Thread. Provided your devices support one of these, you can easily switch a household that’s wholly dependent on Alexa over to the latest Apple device without too much fuss. Not every device supports this standard. Ring is probably the biggest holdout, meaning you won’t be able to check who’s at the door with your HomeView. That won’t be an issue if the HomeView is the first smart home product you’ve invested in, or if you’re more focused on its other features. As you might expect, HomeView is best suited for those deeply invested in Apple’s own services. The £3.7 trillion company told us that it’s built on the same system as CarPlay, which brings your iPhone apps to the infotainment system in your car, so third-party apps will be coming to HomeView soon. But in our brief time with HomeView, there was no Spotify for music streaming, no Audible to finish the chapter of your latest page-turner, and no WhatsApp to join an ongoing video call. History tells us that developers will race to add support to these apps and many more, but as it stands, you’ll need to settle for the Apple-built equivalents. If you want a charming countertop computer that can talk you through each step of a new recipe, dial into FaceTime calls (and keep you in-frame, even as you move around the room), plays music and podcasts from a surprisingly capable set of speakers, keeps tabs on the location of your loved ones (and their devices) via Find My, and offers hands-free access to Siri AI to quickly answer any burning general knowledge questions to settle a debate… HomeView could be the perfect addition to your home. At £299, it’s pretty competitively priced too. Not compared to the ludicrously low price tag you’ll find on Amazon’s Echo Show lineup this Black Friday, of course. But outside of these sales, Echo Show 8 — which has an 8.7-inch screen, the closest to the 7-inch Liquid Retina display on the HomeView — has an RRP of £199.99. Google Nest Hub is much more affordable, costing just £89.99. However, it's worth noting that Google hasn't refreshed that hardware for the last five years, so performance isn't comparable to the brand-new HomeView (let's hope the renewed competition spurs on its teams to finally refresh its ageing hardware...) Compared to other devices lining the shelves of your nearest Apple Store, HomeView seems very reasonable. The new Apple TV 4K box costs £299, and you'll need to spend at least £599 for an iPad mini with a similar-sized screen. HomeView has been a long time coming. Amazon introduced Echo Show back in 2017; that was around the time that Apple was still struggling to keep up with demand for its first-ever AirPods... yes, it's been that long. Now we've seen the HomeView in action, we're confident that families are going to love this clever smart home nerve centre. If you've already invested a lot of money into Ring and other smart home brands that don't play nice with HomeView, you might want to look elsewhere. But those who appreciate the premium fit-and-finish of Apple's products, or who want to access the likes of My Find, Apple Music, and FaceTime from one of these countertop computers won't be disappointed with this new entry. articles.title: Bulgaria Submits 2027 Draft Budgetary Plan to European Commission, Eurogroup with 4.3% Deficit Target
articles.description: Bulgaria’s Finance Ministry submitted its 2027 draft budgetary plan to the European Commission and the Eurogroup, targeting a general government deficit of 4.3% of GDP, the Ministry said on Thursday. The plan includes revenue-raising and expenditure-limiting measures aimed at ending this country’s excessive deficit procedure by 2029. This is Bulgaria’s first budgetary plan as a full member of the euro area, which the country joined on January 1, 2026. The document was submitted by the October 15 deadline and is based on the Finance Ministry’s autumn macroeconomic forecast, approved by the Fiscal Council. For 2026, the Ministry expects an accrual-based deficit of about 5% of GDP, compared with 5.4% envisaged in the State Budget. The 0.4 percentage-point improvement mainly reflects revised Defence Ministry estimates, including changes to military equipment delivery schedules. The projected 2027 deficit of 4.3% represents a 0.7 percentage-point reduction from the updated forecast for this year. Revenue and expenditure are expected to decline as shares of GDP to 36.1% and 40.4%, respectively. Under the EU Council recommendation, Bulgaria should limit annual nominal growth in net expenditure to 4.2% in 2026, 3.4% in both 2027 and 2028, and 3.2% in 2029. Cumulative growth should not exceed 4.2%, 7.7%, 11.4% and 15%, respectively. The aim is to correct the excessive deficit by 2029, taking into account the national escape clause for defence spending activated in 2025. The EU Council opened an excessive deficit procedure for Bulgaria on July 10, 2026. Revenue measures Among the revenue measures is a one-off contribution on windfall profits in selected sectors in 2027, expected to generate an indicative EUR 800 million. The plan also provides for mandatory VAT registration for taxable supplies involving land and buildings and changes to the electronic food voucher regime. Other measures include an excise duty on motor vehicles, changes to the tax on personal use, and updated fines and financial penalties. For the gambling sector, the plan envisages a higher alternative tax on gaming halls and casinos, increased contributions for socially responsible conduct, a state fee on the manufacture and import of gaming equipment, and higher one-off fees for issuing and maintaining gambling licences. It also provides for gradual increases in the variable component of the two-part state fee and a minimum monthly threshold of EUR 100,000 for online gambling operators. Tax and social measures The package also includes tax relief for families with children and businesses, including a higher threshold for mandatory VAT registration, increased tax allowances for children and children with disabilities, and a new child development allowance covering healthcare, education and sports expenses. From January 1, 2027, the maximum contributory income is planned to rise to EUR 2,400, with an estimated revenue effect of EUR 265.1 million. Higher minimum contributory income and minimum insurance thresholds by economic activity and occupational qualification group are expected to bring in another EUR 196.7 million. The plan also provides for dividends from state-owned enterprises and companies with state participation for the 2026 financial year, as well as an interim dividend equal to 50% of reported profit based on six-month financial statements as of June 30, 2027. Expenditure priorities On the expenditure side, pensions are planned to rise by about 8%, public-sector wages by 5% and teachers’ salaries by 7.5%. Child allowances are also set to increase. Additional funding is planned for education, healthcare, culture, sport and security, as well as investment in defence capabilities, including counter-drone and air-defence systems. Structural spending cuts and public-sector administrative optimization launched this year are expected to continue and be completed in 2027. According to the plan, the measures should curb growth in personnel and operating costs while improving the quality of public services. The document also includes reform of the medical disability assessment system to improve expenditure control and measures to encourage public-private partnerships in infrastructure projects. Debt outlook General government debt is projected to reach EUR 40.6 billion at the end of 2026 and EUR 47.1 billion at the end of 2027. The debt-to-GDP ratio is expected to rise from about 31.1% to around 33.3%. The increase is attributed mainly to the need to finance budget deficits, refinance existing debt, raise defence spending and capitalize state-owned companies.

articles.title: ALSTOM S.A: Alstom secures 15-year services contract extension worth nearly 1 billion euro from Greater Anglia in the United Kingdom
articles.description: Alstom will continue to maintain Greater Anglia’s fleet of 133 Class 720 Aventra trains until the early 2040sContract builds on a successful partnership that has delivered one of the UK’s most reliable modern commuter fleetsSupports Greater Anglia with delivering an even better service for its customers and communities during its journey to Great British Railways15 October 2026- Alstom, global leader in smart and sustainable mobility, has signed a 15-year extension to its Train Services Agreement (TSA) with Greater Anglia in the United Kingdom for the operator’s Class 720 Aventra fleet. The contract, valued at approximately 800 million British pounds (947 million euro1), provides continuity for the Aventra fleet and a long-term framework for Alstom, Greater Anglia and future Great British Railways (GBR) to collaborate on performance, reliability and the passenger experience. Under the agreement, Alstom will continue to maintain Greater Anglia’s fleet of 133 five-car Class 720 Aventra electric multiple units (EMUs) at Greater Anglia’s Seven Kings Depot, ensuring the fleet remains available to support intensive commuter and regional services throughout the region. The fleet - financed and owned by Angel Trains - was built at Derby Litchurch Lane Works, one of Alstom’s global Centres of Excellence for rolling stock. The Aventra platform has become a British success story, combining UK design, engineering and manufacturing with strong in-service performance. This long-term agreement marks the next chapter for the Class 720 fleet, supporting Greater Anglia’s objective of delivering an even better service for its customers and communities during its journey to GBR. "We are delighted to extend our partnership with Greater Anglia through this long-term maintenance agreement for the Alstom-built Class 720 fleet. These trains represent one of the most modern commuter fleets in the country, which are already delivering excellent levels of reliability and performance,” said Steve Harvey, Services Director UK and Ireland at Alstom. He added: "This contract reflects the trust that Greater Anglia places in Alstom and demonstrates how the best whole-life outcomes are secured for passengers and taxpayers when owners, operators and manufacturers work in partnership for the long term. We look forward to continuing our collaborative approach to deliver outstanding service for passengers across the region for many years to come.” The TSA covers all planned maintenance activities, including major overhauls, as well as unplanned maintenance, fault rectification, material supply and a comprehensive programme of reliability growth initiatives. The contract also includes the ongoing delivery of performance improvements aimed at maximising fleet availability and supporting Greater Anglia’s operational requirements. The agreement supports around 100 roles at Alstom. Award-Winning Reliability The Class 720 fleet has established a strong reliability performance since entering service, achieving more than 40,000 miles per technical incident (MTIN) in recent periods, significantly exceeding contractual requirements. Meanwhile, in 2024 the trains picked up a Silver Spanner award at the Modern Railways Fourth Friday Club Golden Spanners Awards, meaning they were the most improved train of their type, with a 98.4% year-on-year improvement. "Greater Anglia is pleased to confirm this new 15-year maintenance agreement with Alstom for our fleet of Class 720 trains. We’re looking forward to working with Alstom and Angel Trains to build on the major improvements in service and reliability these new trains have already been delivering for our customers and communities,” said Martin Beable, Chief Operating Officer at GBR Anglia. The Class 720 Aventra fleet was ordered in 2016, alongside the initial TSA, with vehicles entering service progressively over a five-year period. Today, all 133 units are fully operational, delivering modern, accessible and sustainable rail services across the Greater Anglia network, part of GBR Anglia. Alstom has produced 2,660 Aventra cars at its Derby factory for customers across the UK since 2015 - making it the biggest train manufacturing programme in a generation. Proven at scale across England for customers including c2c, Greater Anglia, South Western Railway, Transport for London (for the Elizabeth line and London Overground) and West Midlands Trains (incorporating London Northwestern Railway and West Midlands Railway), Alstom’s Aventra fleets have already delivered over 18 billion passenger miles. The contract with Greater Anglia also reinforces Alstom’s position as a leading provider of long-term rolling stock services in the UK, combining engineering expertise, digital capability and a strong local presence to help customers deliver safe, reliable and sustainable rail services for passengers. Alstom is the market leader in rail services, supporting customers over the entire asset lifecycle with the broadest portfolio of services solutions. Alstom’s FlexCare Perform maintenance services are tailored to customer needs and operational requirements, from technical support with spares to fully outsourced maintenance solutions. Alstom maintains over 36,000 vehicles worldwide and is a trusted partner for servicing both Alstom and non-Alstom rail assets. ALSTOM™, Adessia™, Aventra™ and FlexCare Perform™ are protected trademarks of the Alstom Group. About AlstomAlstom is the pure rail leader, committed to making rail the backbone of sustainable transportation. Alstom designs and delivers a complete range of future-ready solutions - from high-speed and regional trains to metros, monorails, trams, turnkey systems, end-to-end services, infrastructure, signalling and digital rail solutions. With 87,800 people in 61 countries, Alstom brings together global expertise and multi-local presence to make every journey smarter, cleaner and more enjoyable. Together with its partners and customers, Alstom realises the power of rail. Listed in France, Alstom generated revenues of €19.2 billion for the fiscal year ending 31 March 2026. www.alstom.com ContactsPress: HQ Coralie COLLET - T: +33 (0) 7 63 63 09 62 coralie.collet@alstomgroup.com UK and Ireland Ben GOODWIN - T: +44 (0) 7935 348 065 ben.goodwin@alstomgroup.com Investor Relations Cyril GUERIN - T: +33 (0)6 07 89 36 16 cyril.guerin@alstomgroup.com Guillaume GAUVILLE - T: +44 (0)7 588 022 744 guillaume.gauville@alstomgroup.com Jalal DAHMANE - T: +33 (0)6 98 19 96 62 jalal.dahmane@alstomgroup.com 1 This order will be booked in the third quarter of Alstom’s fiscal year 2026/27. articles.title: Currie Slams 'Vibe' Oil Contracts As Trump Admin Halts SPR Drains, IEA Urges Massive Reserve Release
articles.description: Currie Slams 'Vibe' Oil Contracts As Trump Admin Halts SPR Drains, IEA Urges Massive Reserve Release Oil prices are extending gains again this morning as traders weigh a weaker global demand outlook and signs of recovering Middle East crude supplies against persistent shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz and escalating/spreading violence between the Houthis and Saudis. An overnight lull in prices (set with hopes for more reserve releases) was upset as Iran showed more clips of tankers/container ships under attack. The International Energy Agency said Wednesday that Gulf crude shipments rose by 4.4 million barrels a day to 13.9 million barrels a day in September, reaching more than 75% of prewar levels. Global oil supply increased by 2.5 million barrels a day to 102.3 million barrels a day, driven by Gulf producers. However, the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping, the agency said. Given the massive crude draw reported by API (likely impacted by shut-ins from the first Atlantic hurricane of the year in the US Gulf), all eyes are on the (Columbus Day-delayed) official data... API Crude -11.1mm Cushing +1.8mm Gasoline +1.1mm Distillates -1.5mm DOE Crude -8.56mm Cushing +1.86mm Gasoline +3.52mm Distillates -2.52mm HUGE CAVEAT - the shut-ins in the Gulf make this very noisy: Confirming API's reporting, the official data showed a large crude draw last week (and another sizable draw in distillates inventories) while stocks at Cushing and overall Gasoline inventories saw builds... For the first time since the Iran war began, the Trump admin did not drain any reserves from the SPR... US Crude Production tumbled last week (shut-ins in the Gulf, so not comparable)... Total US Diesel stocks remain at seasonal record lows... WTI has surged up to $97.50 However, watching futures is misleading as Wall Street veteran Jeff Currie exclaimed this morning that the world’s most important oil benchmark has become little more than a “vibe contract", blunting its usefulness as a tool to manage price volatility. Brent’s disconnect from physical markets is creating “unpriceable risk,” deterring hedgers from using the contract to protect themselves, Currie said. “Everything associated with energy is going up but Brent,” Currie said Thursday in an interview on Bloomberg Television. “It is not connected to the real world anymore.” A hit to Brent’s integrity undermines the market’s ability to anticipate supply shocks with “profound consequences for the market and the rest of the world,” Currie said. The disconnect between paper and physical markets has frustrated traders since the Middle East conflict began, when crude struggled to top $100 despite historic supply shortages. In contrast, Dated Brent, the most important physical oil benchmark, has surged to near $130 a barrel. That dissonance has contributed to traders fleeing the market, with Brent open interest earlier this month hitting its lowest since March 2025 even as oil dominates headlines. Diesel prices are lower this morning... Finally, Bloomberg reports that US officials attending an International Energy Agency meeting in Paris earlier today informally lobbied allies to commit an additional 100 million barrels from emergency oil inventories to supply global markets. "While US officials attending an IEA gathering in Paris on Thursday have yet to table a proposal about what should be done, they have been informally lobbying for an extra commitment of at least 100 million barrels, the people said, asking not to be identified because the matter is not public." (BBG) The report says US officials believe IEA members have not released enough oil from the coordinated 400 million-barrel oil and fuel release announced in March to cushion the impact of the Gulf conflict. The Group of Seven nations agreed earlier this month to release up to 100 million barrels after President Trump threatened Europeans with a halt to exports of diesel and other petroleum products. Today's request follows Trump's deal with Moscow to supply US and global markets with thousands of tons of diesel fuel. On top of this, a defiant President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times earlier today that his armed forces will attack Russian refineries once again. This comes after the Trump administration requested that Ukraine stop hitting Russian refineries, as those attacks have been one of the drivers of the global refining crisis. Last month, IEA head Fatih Birol said about one-third of the 400 million-barrel release announced in March had been delivered to global markets. Meanwhile, US SPR inventories have fallen to levels not seen since the early 1980s. The Trump administration's scramble comes as midterm elections are just three weeks away. The latest credit and debit card data from Bank of America show that US consumers are spending more on fuel at the pump, crowding out other purchases and weighing on consumer sentiment. articles.title: We've tried Apple HomeView, the smart home hub that iPhone owners have been waiting (a long time) for
articles.description: Apple just unveiled its all-new HomeView alongside a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini 2 speaker during an event in New York City. The showcase was designed to demonstrate how Siri AI, rebuilt from the ground up earlier this summer, can become an essential companion in the home. The smarter, more personal assistant has already changed the way we use our iPhone, thanks to its ability to answer complex open-ended questions and draw from the information stored in your text messages and emails to find specific details that would otherwise take hours of scrolling. With a HomeView on your worktop, bookshelf, bedside table, or mounted on the wall, Siri AI can leverage all of those capabilities to manage your schedule, control smart home gadgets, fire up a playlist or podcast, and be a crib sheet for everything stored on your iPhone. GB News was in Manhattan to be one of the first to see how this works in practice. Apple hasn't strayed from its typical formula with the HomeView. That's to say, this is not the first product of its kind, arriving almost a decade after Amazon announced its first-generation Echo Show smart display, but the Apple-built equivalent arrives with an extraordinary level of finish and best serves those who already heavily invested in its ecosystem of products and services. It's also more expensive than the competition, but more on that later. Since HomeView is designed to take a spot inside your home — ideally somewhere that you're able to easily check and swipe its gorgeous seven-inch Liquid Retina display — design is particularly important. The most striking thing about HomeView is how adorable it is. That might sound like an odd thing to say about a gadget, but its small stature and cherubic rounded display ensure there's something incredibly endearing about the HomeView. That touchscreen is connected to the half-dome speaker with a sturdy stainless steel hinge that tilts so you can avoid any troublesome glare. The wall-mounted version drops the speaker in the base and relies only on those around the display to play music. HomeView is surprisingly small, and wouldn't look out of place on a bedside or coffee table. Those who want to gather around as a family to use the Centre Stage camera, which ensures everyone remains in-frame even as they move around, for a FaceTime call might find themselves longing for more screen real estate, as Amazon offers with its Echo Show 11. When it's not in use, HomeView has a series of beautifully designed clock faces. Many of these will be immediately familiar to Apple Watch owners. There are endless customisation options, including the font, colours, and complications to offer weather conditions, world clock, and upcoming calendar appointments at a glance. Between the 1:1 aspect ratio, rounded corners, and shared clock faces with its bestselling smartwatch, HomeView can resemble a supersized Apple Watch. One of the available options will spotlight photos from your library. You can even set a Shared iCloud Album as the source of these photos, so family members or friends can upload recent additions, refreshing multiple HomeViews — even those in different households — with new pictures. Like the Lock Screen on your iPhone, subjects are automatically separated from the background, ensuring the date and time never obscure someone's face. Given most of us have thousands of photos on our smartphones that we never really look at, HomeView could be a nice hassle-free way to be reminded of some choice memories. Like the Apple Watch and Apple TV, Snoopy makes a very welcome appearance on HomeView. There's a series of custom animations that play, with the weather on-screen reflecting the conditions outside. Likewise, Snoopy will celebrate certain holidays — Christmas, for example — on the HomeView at the same time as you. It's a fun addition, and will please younger members of the household and big kids alike. For our money, we would've loved to see the Toy Story cast as well as Micky and Minnie Mouse enjoy their own clock face too, since these Disney staples have all made appearances on the Apple Watch in the past. Likewise, some of the breathtaking aerial footage that serves as a screensaver on Apple TV would look stunning on this photo frame-like display, serving as a digital version of the 1,000 Places To See Before You Die daily tear-off desk calendar. Fingers crossed the teams at Apple regularly refresh the selection of clock faces available on HomeView. Software updates — bringing new features and security fixes — will be delivered via the Home app preinstalled on your iPhone or iPad, like the HomePod smart speakers already available from the brand. HomeView walks a tricky tightrope — it needs to be personal enough to be useful for everyone living under the same roof, but secure and private enough that you're confident allowing it to display your texts or manage your reminders. To solve this, HomeView has several safeguards. First, it boasts facial recognition for up to six people. But that's not enough, so Apple also checks that your iPhone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network (or, failing that, in roughly the same location as the HomeView) and has been recently unlocked. HomeView doesn't come equipped with Face ID — the facial recognition system used to unlock most iPhones and authenticate contactless payments — so the extra precautions ensure someone can't use a photograph to trick the camera and unlock access to your personal data when you're not home. However, its absence is not a case of Apple skimping on components. Face ID works by projecting some 30,000 invisible infrared dots onto your face and checking the unique curves, angles, and distances between your facial features. This isn't a three-dimensional scan, but instead takes the form of mathematical data for all of this geometry. Given that HomeView is designed to be used from across the room, rather than at arm's length — like an iPhone or iPad, this projection system isn't suitable. During our demo, profiles switched over instantaneously whenever someone new walked up to the HomeView. A notification flags when a new profile has been signed in. With so much concern about AI, should you trust Siri to access everything on your iPhone? HomeView has an elegant solution to nosiness from other members of your household. If someone peers at the screen while you're composing a text, for example, the display will automatically lock, GB News was told. This system also serves as a way to make sure everyone enjoys a personalised experience. Like an iPhone, you can customise the appearance and layout of apps and add widgets, so each member of your household can add their own flourish to the device. This all appears the moment that HomeView recognises you. Likewise, playlists in Apple Music, photo libraries, podcasts, and other in-app data will appear when you swipe the touchscreen or use Siri AI on the HomeView. Some experiences — like the ability to customise the colour or brightness of smart lightbulbs, or check a doorbell camera feed — are always accessible to everyone. This isn't entirely new. Both Google Nest and Amazon Echo devices offer personalised experiences, so you can send text messages to your contacts and add items to your calendar, without allowing anyone at home to access. But these services rely on voice recognition to sort you from the rest of your household. Alexa Voice ID data — the acoustic model of your voice characteristics — is stored on Amazon's servers, something that might put you off using this feature. And unlike the HomeView, there's nothing to stop prying eyes. HomeView has a couple of unique tricks up its sleeve too. Handoff lets you beam a song, podcast, or audiobook from your iPhone to the HomeView. Just hold your phone in front of the display, and you'll see a splash animation as if you've physically thrown something into the screen. HomeView will pick-up at the exact spot where you left off. The inverse too, letting you take a song or episode with you when you leave the house. Like the jaw-dropping animation when you open the iPhone Duo, GB News was left seriously impressed with this beautiful flourish. It is impeccably executed and adds to a seamless cohesion between these devices, helpful when you've invested in multiple gadgets from the same brand. Another example of these nice touches is the cooking experience with HomeView. If you find a recipe in its Safari web browser, onboard Artificial Intelligence (AI) will detect that it's a recipe and distil all of the information into an easily digestible, step-by-step format that you can follow in the kitchen when your hands are busy. If the recipe mentions timings, Apple will add shortcuts to kickstart a timer for that designated time. You'll be able to see a countdown in real-time of exactly how long is left at the top of the screen, similar to the Dynamic Island on iPhone. iPhone 18 Pro review HomeView will pull out the list of ingredients too, and using the power of Siri AI, you can ask the chatty assistant to add these to your shopping list, remind you to buy a particular item when you're near the local supermarket. HomeView is available in four colours: Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, Space Grey. However, that drops to just two — Silver and Space Grey — if you choose the wall-mounted version. While both versions of the HomeView cost the same at checkout, the wall-mounted one requires extra hardware to attach to the wall. Apple has created three purpose-built mounts, ranging from £54.95 to £119.95. That makes this a much more expensive proposition, and while the company reassured GB News it has tuned the audio to bounce soundwaves off the wall to preserve audio quality ...the fact that it's missing the drivers in the base must result in a weaker output. Early Verdict There’s no shortage of ways to manage smart lightbulbs, thermostats, or security cameras. And if you’ve ever browsed Amazon during the Black Friday sales, you’ll know the US retailer is prepared to offer some aggressive discounts to tempt you into its own ecosystem, which includes a paid subscription to its smarter Alexa+ assistant, Ring doorbells, and Blink security cameras. Likewise, Google has its own Nest Hub smart display and security cameras. There are standards that mean you can use these devices interchangeably. HomeView supports the two biggest ones: Matter and Thread. Provided your devices support one of these, you can easily switch a household that’s wholly dependent on Alexa over to the latest Apple device without too much fuss. Not every device supports this standard. Ring is probably the biggest holdout, meaning you won’t be able to check who’s at the door with your HomeView. That won’t be an issue if the HomeView is the first smart home product you’ve invested in, or if you’re more focused on its other features. As you might expect, HomeView is best suited for those deeply invested in Apple’s own services. The £3.7 trillion company told us that it’s built on the same system as CarPlay, which brings your iPhone apps to the infotainment system in your car, so third-party apps will be coming to HomeView soon. But in our brief time with HomeView, there was no Spotify for music streaming, no Audible to finish the chapter of your latest page-turner, and no WhatsApp to join an ongoing video call. History tells us that developers will race to add support to these apps and many more, but as it stands, you’ll need to settle for the Apple-built equivalents. If you want a charming countertop computer that can talk you through each step of a new recipe, dial into FaceTime calls (and keep you in-frame, even as you move around the room), plays music and podcasts from a surprisingly capable set of speakers, keeps tabs on the location of your loved ones (and their devices) via Find My, and offers hands-free access to Siri AI to quickly answer any burning general knowledge questions to settle a debate… HomeView could be the perfect addition to your home. At £299, it’s pretty competitively priced too. Not compared to the ludicrously low price tag you’ll find on Amazon’s Echo Show lineup this Black Friday, of course. But outside of these sales, Echo Show 8 — which has an 8.7-inch screen, the closest to the 7-inch Liquid Retina display on the HomeView — has an RRP of £199.99. Google Nest Hub is much more affordable, costing just £89.99. However, it's worth noting that Google hasn't refreshed that hardware for the last five years, so performance isn't comparable to the brand-new HomeView (let's hope the renewed competition spurs on its teams to finally refresh its ageing hardware...) Compared to other devices lining the shelves of your nearest Apple Store, HomeView seems very reasonable. The new Apple TV 4K box costs £299, and you'll need to spend at least £599 for an iPad mini with a similar-sized screen. HomeView has been a long time coming. Amazon introduced Echo Show back in 2017; that was around the time that Apple was still struggling to keep up with demand for its first-ever AirPods... yes, it's been that long. Now we've seen the HomeView in action, we're confident that families are going to love this clever smart home nerve centre. If you've already invested a lot of money into Ring and other smart home brands that don't play nice with HomeView, you might want to look elsewhere. But those who appreciate the premium fit-and-finish of Apple's products, or who want to access the likes of My Find, Apple Music, and FaceTime from one of these countertop computers won't be disappointed with this new entry.
